correctness.rationale: The proof derives an exact inclusion/two-hop equivalence, independent ternary conditional coordinate distribution with covariance 1/9, vanishing shared-index local-dependence errors O(m^3(3/4)^(2n)+m^3(5/8)^n+m^2(1/2)^n), and a direct union bound for the diameter reduction. Under m^2(3/4)^n -> lambda in (0,infinity), all errors vanish; standard multivariate Stein-Chen and the bivariate CLT finish the marked process. The standalone checker passed 79,561 finite assertions. Infinite results do not rely on that enumeration.

originality.rationale: The unmarked Poisson comparison-count law and conditional one-pair ternary coordinates are known from Stark (2004) and expressly excluded from the novelty claim. The assessed addition is independent Gaussian marks across the rare exceptional process and a sharp directed diameter-three/four mixture with an all-finite-parameter routing error estimate. Searches did not identify the full combined statement, but some older primary texts remain inaccessible; priority is qualified.
residual_risks: Stark (2004) contains the full unmarked count theorem and the one-pair conditional coordinate distribution: any stronger novelty claim for those is precluded.
The Moon–Moser (1962) and Bollobás–Frank–Karoński (1983) original texts were unavailable for a full claim-level search; a deeper historical review could discover prior stronger coverage.

General marked rare-event Poisson point-process approximation theorems may yield the marked part after model-specific computation, reducing novelty; the directed global diameter reduction remains an explicit additional assertion.

value.rationale: The 3-versus-4 directed diameter phase at exponential bipartition imbalance is a motivated natural network invariant. The marked result identifies that rare diameter failure is caused by source/target outward degrees near n/3 and 2n/3 with correlated Gaussian fluctuations, not ordinary vertices near n/2; it also gives the location law and a finite global-routing error bound. This is more than a new parametrization of the known unmarked count distribution.
